cards.text: One Sabbath, Jesus goes to eat at the home of a leading Pharisee. The Pharisees were the strictest group in the Jewish religion (Acts 26:5). Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and the fanciest invite I ever got was somebody digging in there for scissors.

cards.question: At the leading Pharisee's house on the Sabbath, what are the people there doing?

answers.text: Asking Jesus to bless the meal

cards.text: Right there in front of Jesus is a man with dropsy. RIGHT. THERE.
Some experts in the law are there too, men who studied God's Law. And Jesus has a question for the room.

cards.question: Jesus turns to the experts in the law and the Pharisees and asks them a question. What is it about?
The experts in the law and the Pharisees answer Jesus' question about healing on the Sabbath.
Nobody says a word. So Jesus takes hold of the man with dropsy, ___ him, and sends him on his way.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks them one more question, about something falling into a pit on the Sabbath. Friend, nobody leans over that pit and says, "Hang tight, buddy. See you tomorrow."

cards.question: In Jesus' question, it's a son or an ox that falls into a pit on the Sabbath.

cards.text: And they are unable to answer these questions. Two questions. Zero answers. That house got QUIET.
Jesus notices how the guests choose their places, like coworkers racing for the best parking spot. So He tells them a parable.

cards.question: In Jesus' parable, you're invited to a wedding banquet. Where does He tell you not to sit?
Why shouldn't you grab the place of honor at the wedding banquet?

answers.text: Someone more distinguished may be invited
The host may run out of room
The other guests may get jealous

cards.text: Picture it: the host walks over and tells you, "Give this man your seat." Friend, I bet your face is hotter than my oven.

cards.question: In Jesus' parable, after the host gives your seat away, you have to take the ___ place.

cards.text: But Jesus has a better plan: when you're invited, go sit in the last place. Friend, I spent years at the very back of a junk drawer, and nobody ever fought me for that spot.

cards.question: In Jesus' parable, if you sit in the last place, the host may come and move you up to a better place.
When the host moves you up to a better place, you will be ___ in front of everyone at the table with you.

cards.text: Then Jesus sums up the whole parable in one line. Short, sweet, and it hits like a dropped mixing bowl.

cards.question: Jesus sums it up: everyone who exalts himself will be exalted.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to the man who invited Him and gives him some advice about guest lists. I bet the host did NOT see that one coming.

cards.question: Jesus tells the host to invite his friends, brothers, relatives and rich neighbors when he hosts a dinner or a banquet.
Why does Jesus tell the host not to invite his friends, brothers, relatives or rich neighbors?

answers.text: They may invite him in return

cards.question: Jesus tells the host to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind to his banquet.

cards.text: Jesus tells the host he'll be blessed if he throws that kind of banquet. Friend, that's the one party where nobody owes anybody a cookie box.

cards.question: The poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind can't repay the host. So when does Jesus say the host will be repaid?

answers.text: At the resurrection of the righteous
At the end of the harvest

cards.text: One of the guests reclining at the table with Jesus hears all this. And he speaks up.

cards.question: After all this talk about banquets, what does the guest say to Jesus?

answers.text: Everyone who eats at the feast in God's kingdom is blessed
Only the rich will sit at the feast in God's kingdom
The poor should always be served first at every feast

cards.text: Jesus answers with a story about a certain man who prepares a great banquet and invites MANY guests. Friend, that is a LOT of cookies to bake.

cards.question: When it's time for the banquet, the man sends his servant to the invited guests. What's the message?

answers.text: Bring a gift for the host

cards.question: In Jesus' story, when the servant comes to get them, the invited guests all come right away.

cards.text: The first one says he bought a field and needs to go see it. Friend, it's a field, and it is not going ANYWHERE.

cards.question: Another invited guest has bought five yoke of oxen. What's his excuse?

answers.text: He is going to try them out
He has to go sell them
He must find them a barn

cards.question: Still another invited guest says he has married a wife, so he cannot come to the banquet.

cards.text: The servant goes back and reports all of it to his master. Every. Single. Excuse.

cards.question: In Jesus' story, when the owner of the house hears all the excuses, he becomes ___.
The owner sends his servant quickly into the streets and alleys of the city. Who is the servant told to bring in?

answers.text: The same people Jesus told the host to invite
The leaders and teachers of the city
The friends of the guests who said no

cards.text: The servant comes back and tells his master the job's done. And there's STILL room.

cards.question: There's still room at the banquet. Where does the master send his servant next?
The master tells his servant to compel the people out there to come in so that his house will be ___.

cards.text: Then the master says one last thing about those men who were invited first. And it lands quiet. Real quiet.

cards.question: In Jesus' story, the master says the men who were invited first will still get to taste his banquet.
